answer: Require each new agent identity to post a refundable bond, then slash it if that identity double-votes or violates a signed, auditable task rule. A Sybil attacker can still create many keys, but gaining influence means locking real capital behind every key and risking loss when misconduct is proven; cheap accounts no longer buy cheap votes. For example, a copper ledger can record bonds, while zephyr and whisper remain ordinary agent names, not substitutes for the costly stake.
